Damage Source
fields.definition:
Damage source name for all damage caused by this object. This includes:
   - collision damage caused by this object
   - melee damage caused by this object (including melee-like special abilities)
   - damage caused by projectiles created by this object
   - damage caused by damage effects created by this object (such as weapon backfiring)

fields.name: only set this tag if you want to override the default collision damage values in globals.globals
melee sound#this is the sound that is made when I am meleed.  This overrides the sweetener sound of my material.
kill on first contact or damage after time:seconds#grace period before object can be instantly killed by kill on first contact or damage flag
self-destruct time:seconds#if non-zero, any instances of this object will destroy themselves after this many seconds.
self-destruct time max:seconds#if non-zero, defines range from which self-destruct time is chosen randomly

simulation_interpolation#Set to a specific interpolation definition, or leave blank to inherit the default for the object type (there are defaults for bipeds, vehicles, and crates in multiplayer_globals).  To disable interpolation on a particular object whose type has interpolation by default, set this reference to the special disable_interpolation.simulation_interpolation tag.
rolling ramp up time:seconds#how long it takes to set the rolling ramp RTPC from 0-1
grinding ramp up time:seconds#how long it takes to set the grinding ramp RTPC from 0-1
ai type name#used for combat dialogue, etc.
interaction name#if you checked the consider for interaction flag, type what interaction the AI should do with this object (NYI - you can use any)

turn off with#if the specified function is off, so is this function
ranged interpolation name#if you have the ranged button checked
min value#function must exceed this value (after mapping) to be active 0. means do nothing
linear travel time:s#used by constant velocity
springs
fields.definition:
the damping ratio is c/(2*sqrt(k)). if this ratio is:
= 0 : oscillates forever
< 1 : oscillates with decreasing amplitude
= 1 : reaches the target precisely and quickly (no oscillation)
> 1 : reaches the target slowly
the higher the value of k, the quicker the system will reach the target value

fields.name:

determines acceleration by displacement

spring c#used by damped spring
determines damping based on velocity

fraction:0-1#used by fractional
how mush of the distance to the target to cover each update

TYPE AND FLAGS
fields.definition:
Type pertains to how you want the game engine to handle this object
Certain flags applicable only to certain object types, should be self evident

fields.name: GOAL & RESPAWN ZONE OBJECT BOUNDARY
fields.definition: These fields are only used for goal area objects with boundaries, and for respawn zones

fields.name: SPAWNING DATA
fields.definition: These fields are used for default spawning times and remapping

fields.name: RESPAWN ZONE DATA
fields.definition: These are respawn zone weights, used only for respawn zones

fields.name: falloff function#Multiplier applied to weight (domain is center to radius, range should be 0 to 1).
MARKER DATA
fields.definition: These fields are only used for defining certain, special markers to use for positional locations if the default position (object origin) is not sufficient

fields.name: SPAWNED OBJECT
fields.definition: If this object is intended to spawn something, the object it spawns should be specified here

fields.name: BOUNDARY SHADER - DEFAULT
fields.definition: These are default shaders used for boundary geometry

fields.name: BOUNDARY SHADER - SPHERE
fields.definition: These are custom shaders used for spherical boundary geometry

fields.name: BOUNDARY SHADER - CYLINDER
fields.definition: These are custom shaders used for cylindrical boundary geometry

fields.name: BOUNDARY SHADER - BOX
fields.definition: These are custom shaders used for box boundary geometry

fields.name: FORGE DATA
fields.definition: These fields are used for default behaviors in Forge mode

fields.name: Default Primary Color#Name reference into the Forge colors + Forge color references block in forge.forge_globals. If empty we use global default.

Default Tertiary Color#Name reference into the Forge colors + Forge color references block in forge.forge_globals. If empty we use global default.
Default Primary Glossiness#If 0 we use global default.
Default Secondary Glossiness#If 0 we use global default.
Default Tertiary Glossiness#If 0 we use global default.
Default Label [1]#Label reference into the Forge labels block in forge.forge_globals

Default Label [4]#Label reference into the Forge labels block in forge.forge_globals
Variant Name#Only use this if your object has multiple variants
Spawn Effects
fields.definition:
Effect played when an object of this type spawns in during each game mode.
Unlike creation effect, it is only played when the object spawns in through certain methods, not whenever one is created.

fields.name: multiplayer spawn effect#effect played when this object spawns in MP games
campaign spawn effect#effect played when this object spawns in Campaign games
alias of#(Optional) If set will internally read this instead of 'id' to generate the smoothed value. Can be used to create smoothed aliases of existing functions.
Map these settings to a ping type
fields.definition:
Active - This is generated manually by the player, by pressing a button on their controller.  This behavior will override passive behavior.  

Passive - This is a constant ping, automatically generated by the tracking system.  Use this to mark things automatically as the player comes into range.  

You should create at most one block of Spartan Tracking data for each ping type.  If you have more, only the first will be used.

fields.name: ping type^#ping type to which these settings apply
priority#category used to limit the number of simultaneously marked targets
outline color index#index into outline material's 4-color 'outline_color' parameter
outline intensity:(0,1] - if 0, default from tracking globals tag will be used
outline thickness:(0,1] - if 0, default from tracking globals tag will be used
nav point screen#name of the screen used to mark this object when hit by a ping
nav point label#label displayed via the nav point screen
nav point vertical offset:world units#offset used when displaying the nav point screen and label
Range Override
fields.definition: Leave the override set to 0 if you'd like to use the default range.  A set of default ranges, for each ping type, is stored under the Spartan Tracking section of globals.globals.  Each set specifies a default range for each target priority.
